summary: My v1 finding is properly repaired and I re-measured the register rather than accepting the restatement: DR-002 through DR-007 do carry HARD-BLOCKED and DR-008 PARTIALLY SATISFIED, and the repair goes further than asked by adding a guard clause and a matching attack line so the error cannot recur silently. The new D-002 material is accurate too - COORDINATOR-DECISIONS says DR-106, DR-109 and DR-113 are deferred WHOLLY - and it is correctly firewalled from being read as a SATISFY or a D-096 (A) grant. All carries remain byte-exact, the mid-sentence boundary is still disclosed, no commit/CAS/ledger API is invented, and reMeasurementAtV1 was demoted honestly rather than left claiming currency. Two defects stop it, both introduced by this successor. First, /recordedInputs changed - the COORD pin's digest and its role prose were both rewritten - and it is not on the declared eleven-path roster, so the method's closing sentence that every unnamed path is unchanged from v1 is false of v2's own bytes. The new values are truthful, which is why this is a roster defect rather than a smuggling one; but the roster is exactly the guarantee a reviewer certifies, and this successor was otherwise scrupulous about it, even adding a Standing rule for demoted blocks. Second, the append repeats v1's closing line verbatim, so 'Do not mark DR-109 SATISFIED. Never mint a D-096 (A) grant.' now sits at both index 8 and index 11; v1 had no duplicates. That is the same duplicate-guidance defect the sibling DR-101 artifact spent three generations removing, and which I found re-introduced there at v15 - two families now showing the same append habit. Both fixes are one line each.
